run.executedVia: Playwright runner, no browser: ServiceNow read over cnit and the Scripted REST API as sf.integration, Salesforce read over the sf CLI and anonymous Apex against the deployed classes. Every case reads both sides.

case.title: Columns are derived from data, not hard-coded

steps.text: List the active CAF Controls — the ServiceNow column source.
List the distinct controls present in the mirrored request data — the Salesforce column source.

records.label: Controls represented in Salesforce request data

observations: Neither LWC nor widget hard-codes a column list: cafDashboard.build() collects distinct CAF_Control__c from the returned rows and sorts them, so a new control needs no code change on either side.

The two sources legitimately disagree, and Sync Health will not report it — no mirrored record disagrees, because the control table is not mirrored. Anyone comparing the two grid screenshots without this note will raise the difference as a defect.

Part B — introducing a request against a control not currently represented, and confirming a column appears with no code change — is ONE-SHOT and needs a write to ServiceNow. Not executed in this pass.
expected: The ServiceNow grid draws columns from caf_conformance_type where active=true.
The Salesforce LWC draws columns from the CAF_Request__c data it holds; no control object is mirrored.
A control with no requests gets a column in ServiceNow and none in Salesforce.
actual: ServiceNow column set (6): Confirm & Execute High Availability Plan, Confirm Backup & Restore Policy, Confirm Disaster Recovery Plan, Confirm RTO & RPO, Test Backup & Restore, Test Disaster Recovery Plan

Salesforce column set (6): Confirm & Execute High Availability Plan, Confirm Backup & Restore Policy, Confirm Disaster Recovery Plan, Confirm RTO & RPO, Test Backup & Restore, Test Disaster Recovery Plan
Columns ServiceNow would show and Salesforce would not: none
Columns Salesforce would show and ServiceNow would not: none
case.verdictReason: Both grids currently derive the same column set from data. The divergence the case documents is latent, not present: every active control happens to have at least one request. Part B not executed (ONE-SHOT).
